must_contain: Issued on 14 July 2026 to the operations leadership group.
This review covers the six direct-material suppliers that delivered more than 50 shipments
Delivery performance is measured against the confirmed delivery date.
Defect rates are given in parts per million (ppm) of received parts.
Average on-time delivery improved from 91.4 percent in the first quarter to 93.8 percent in the second quarter
while the average defect rate fell from 412 to 365 ppm.
Table 1. On-time delivery and defect rate by supplier, first half 2026
Dunmore Electronics remains on conditional status until its defect rate stays below 500 ppm
Delivery performance improved at every supplier in the second quarter.
Bexley Fasteners gained 3.2 points after moving to weekly call-offs.
Dunmore Electronics gained 3.8 points but is still below the 90 percent target.
Most late shipments were linked to a single connector family.
Defect rates fell at five of the six suppliers.
Corran Plastics was the exception, rising from 365 to 372 ppm.
No supplier was moved to a lower rating during the period.
Dunmore Electronics to submit a revised control plan by 31 July 2026.
The plan must cover incoming inspection of the connector family.
Northbank quality engineers will audit the plan on site in August.
Bexley Fasteners to extend weekly call-offs to the Coventry plant.
Procurement to renew the Arden Castings and Elstree Coatings agreements for two years.
Table 2. Cost of poor quality by plant, first half 2026 (GBP)
The total cost of poor quality for the half year was £48,860, of which scrap accounted for 60.6 percent.
The next review is scheduled for January 2027 and will include the two new casting suppliers.
Suppliers with fewer than 50 shipments in the period are reviewed once a year instead.
The 500 ppm threshold was agreed with the supplier in the 2025 quality agreement.
Returns are valued at the replacement cost charged back to the supplier.
